identity.title: Stimulant/substance exposure: caffeine, energy drinks, decongestants, beta-agonists, cocaine/amphetamines, alcohol binge (holiday heart), recent withdrawal

technique.how: Ask non-judgementally about daily caffeine (coffee, energy drinks, pre-workout supplements), nicotine/vaping, OTC decongestants and diet pills, beta-agonists, thyroid hormone, cocaine, amphetamines/MDMA, cannabis, and alcohol pattern (binge in the past 24-48 h; abrupt cessation of alcohol, benzodiazepines or beta-blockers). Time each exposure against palpitation onset.
technique.prerequisites: Privacy; corroborate with medication list and, where indicated, urine toxicology and alcohol level; ECG at the time of symptoms if available.

interpretation.positive_finding: Palpitations beginning within hours of a stimulant, sympathomimetic or binge-drinking exposure, or 1-3 days into alcohol/sedative/beta-blocker withdrawal, support secondary sinus tachycardia, ectopy or alcohol-associated AF ('holiday heart').
interpretation.negative_finding: No exposure makes a substance-triggered mechanism unlikely but says nothing about primary arrhythmia, thyroid disease or anxiety.
interpretation.pitfalls: Exposure is common and mostly coincidental, so a substance history cannot substitute for rhythm documentation; cocaine and amphetamines also cause ischemia, VT and aortic dissection, and alcohol AF often recurs without ongoing intake. Patients under-report illicit and alcohol use.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: obtain ECG/rhythm capture, toxicology or alcohol level as indicated, counsel cessation and reassess; negative: focus on documented arrhythmia, thyroid, anemia and anxiety.

sources.citation: Weber BE, Kapoor WN. Evaluation and outcomes of patients with palpitations. Am J Med. 1996.
Ettinger PO, Wu CF, De La Cruz C, Weisse AB, et al. Arrhythmias and the "Holiday Heart": alcohol-associated cardiac rhythm disorders. Am Heart J. 1978.
Zimetbaum P, Josephson ME. Evaluation of patients with palpitations. N Engl J Med. 1998.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attribute palpitations to caffeine or alcohol when there is syncope, exertional onset, chest pain, structural heart disease, family history of sudden death or an abnormal ECG.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Sympathomimetic toxicity with chest pain, hyperthermia, hypertension or wide-complex tachycardia, and alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal with delirium or seizures, need emergency management.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No inter-observer data; self-reported substance use is systematically under-reported.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy study of a stimulant/alcohol history for the cause of palpitations was found. Weber & Kapoor 1996 (190 consecutive patients, prospective cohort, university medical center) describe the etiologic spectrum: 'The etiology of palpitations was cardiac in 43%, psychiatric in 31%, miscellaneous in 10%, and unknown in 16%' and 'Forty percent of the etiologies could be determined with the history and physical examination, an electrocardiogram, and/or laboratory data' (Abstract, Results); they do not report the accuracy of the substance history. Ettinger 1978 (holiday heart) and Zimetbaum 1998 (NEJM review) have no PubMed abstract and are cited as descriptive/consensus context. Status not_quantified; no numeric estimate entered.
